2. THESIS REVISION: Compare your W131 thesis with your initial ideas from W129. Has your position changed after research? Why?
3. CAMBRIDGE PET: Reading Part 3 practice — Read an article about smartphone bans in schools. Answer True/False/Not Given for 7 statements.

parts.title: PART 1: READING INPUT  BUILDING THE CASE AGAINST SMARTPHONES
content: The strongest argumentative essays do NOT avoid the opposing side — they engage with it. Today, we research the three main arguments AGAINST children having smartphones, so we can address them in our essays.
ARGUMENT 1 — MENTAL HEALTH RISKS: Studies show that heavy smartphone use is linked to increased anxiety, depression, and low self-esteem in children, especially due to social media.
ARGUMENT 2 — DISTRACTION & ACADEMIC PERFORMANCE: Research by UNESCO found that schools banning smartphones saw a 6% improvement in test scores, with the biggest gains for disadvantaged students.

ARGUMENT 3 — ONLINE DANGERS: Children are vulnerable to cyberbullying, inappropriate content, and online predators. The Internet Watch Foundation reports millions of child protection incidents annually.
(↑ Re-read the story above to answer:)
T / F: The text is about building the case against smartphones.

parts.title: PART 8: MY PORTFOLIO ENTRY — PROJECT DRAFT  📝  Week 131 — Session 1
content: Sentence 1: For each anti-smartphone argument, find ONE piece of evidence. Take notes in CLAIM + EVIDENCE + EXPLANATION format (same as W130).
Sentence 2: DECIDE YOUR POSITION. After researching both sides:
Sentence 3: - Which side do you find more convincing overall?
